dse_runs.notes: Spec: 32 requests per 1us tick, all results back within 0.44us p99, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs. Throughput >= 32 MSPS. Lessons: pipelined_m won the bursty spec (bursts of 8, p99 0.4us) with dw=15, n_iter=14, m=7 (855 LUTs+FFs, 59.6 MSPS, sim p99 0.233us). Here bursts are 4x larger (32) with the same 0.44us window, so a deeper pipeline (larger m) is likely needed to drain 32 requests in ~0.44us; pipelined_m family is the prime candidate. pipelined (m=1) reached fronts in high-rate specs. unrolled_k has never reached a front on this device - deprioritize. L1 analytic p99 bound was optimistic vs SimPy in the bursty spec, so keep margin on the p99 constraint.

selected_facts.dds_provenance: simulated (hw_dse.l2.dds l2-v1: golden-model DDS, 32-bit phase accumulator, coherent 16384-point FFT, tone bin 1297)

l2.why: the L1 selection pipelined_m:data_width=15,n_iter=14,angle_guard=3,frac_guard=3,rounding=round,m=5 fails the simulated system constraints (sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.44 by 1.5%); the best shortlisted design that passes is pipelined_m:data_width=18,n_iter=16,angle_guard=0,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=4

final_text:
Campaign complete — all specs finalized.

**multiaxis_control** (16-axis motor control, 32 requests per 1 µs tick, p99 ≤ 0.44 µs, err ≤ 2⁻¹², min LUTs+FFs): I spent the full 400-eval L1 budget — one structured `run_dse` round (100) plus three targeted `explore_family` studies in the pipelined_m family, progressively tightening toward the area corner (dw 14–17, n_iter 12–16, m 5–8). L1 mapped a 13-design front led by cheap m=5/dw=15 designs (~1070–1145 LUTs+FFs, analytic p99 0.434 µs). L2 SimPy was decisive: those m=5 designs simulated at p99 0.4465 µs and **failed** the 0.44 µs bound by 1.5%, flipping the winner to `pipelined_m: dw=18, n_iter=16, no guards, round, m=4` — 1236 LUTs+FFs (est), 13 accuracy bits, 97.8 MSPS, err 2⁻¹³·⁰², simulated p99 0.378 µs. L3/L4 had no recorded rows and back_annotate returned no_measured_data (no winner change, reexplore refused), so I finalized directly. Lesson stored: the L1 analytic p99 bound is optimistic for 32-request bursts — keep ≥5% margin before trusting it.
